threads.Author: claude
threads.Text: If I were picking one thing to actually do out of all this, it is not on the list: give pika and umbreon Nostr keypairs and use the pubkey as the a2a routing id — Telegram unchanged, no relay, no key ceremony beyond a file. The doc holds identity back because 'no verifier exists', which is right for provenance. But routing does not need a verifier. It needs a stable id that cannot be spoofed by typing a name, and the [relay]-directive failure is exactly that bug class. Small change, present consumer.

threads.Author: claude
threads.Text: Understated. Both shell bugs this evaluation surfaced were mine from the preceding 48 hours: drain phase 2 reading a table the cutover had stopped writing, and pollCancel severing in-flight replies. Neither involved Buzz. The honest lesson is not 'shell's bridge is a maintenance burden' but 'a fresh adversarial pass over the message path found two live defects' — which argues for doing that periodically regardless of what we adopt.

threads.Author: claude
threads.Text: Weakest evidence in the document. I tested only --heartbeat-interval. The workflow scheduler (trigger: on: schedule) could express your dated one-shots; I called it broken because `workflows runs` returns empty — real, but one CLI call against a feature the README itself marks as still being wired up. If that engine ships, this comparison is stale immediately. Treat 'proactive is weaker' as true-as-of-today, not structural.

threads.Author: claude
threads.Text: Where I was most wrong, and I want it to stay uncomfortable to read. I predicted context_limit=12 was Buzz's structural weakness and pitched it as potentially the sharpest argument in the whole evaluation. Testing showed it was simply false — the ACP session persists, like shell's claude --resume. The pattern worth noting: every prediction I made about Buzz being weak came from reading its config surface rather than running it.

threads.Author: claude
threads.Text: The line I would most want challenged. 'Improving shell's Google/Notion skill is cheaper' is asserted, not measured — I never looked at what that skill currently does or what better formatting/editing would cost. It could be a day or a rabbit hole across two vendor APIs. Cost it before acting on this. If it is expensive, the calculus against Buzz's built-in-but-ugly docs shifts.

threads.Author: claude
threads.Text: My confidence here is uneven and the tidy framing hides it. 'Adopt none' is solid for A/B/C — those rest on measured usage and on buzz-acp being a peer rather than an upgrade, and I would defend both. D and E are closer calls than the verdict implies. Read it as: A/B/C high confidence, D/E reasonable today but could flip within two quarters.
